KIDS GAMES LESSON · KIDS GAMES · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Duck, Duck, Goose — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches duck, duck, goose — the circle game that every party and every playground already knows.

What is this?

Duck, duck, goose is a circle game: one player walks around tapping heads saying "duck" — until they pick a goose, and the chase is on.

What does it mean?

The game teaches the wait-and-go switch: sitting players hold still, and the goose must burst into running at one exact word.

What does the child need to know?

You need three or more players and floor space for a circle. No equipment at all — the circle and the words are the whole game.

Why this matters

It is the fairest running game for mixed ages: the tapper walks, the goose runs, and every child gets both jobs in one round.

What it teaches

Turn-taking, impulse control (waiting while heads get tapped), sprinting, and the social art of choosing a goose kindly.

Words to learn

circleduckgoosetaprunchasespot

Say this to your child

“"Duck... duck... duck... GOOSE! Run, run, run around the ring! Reach the spot and sit down before the goose catches you!"”

Step by step

  1. Everyone sits cross-legged in a circle, knees almost touching.
  2. One player is the tapper — everyone else is a sitting duck.
  3. The tapper walks around the outside, tapping each head: "duck... duck... duck..."
  4. On one head the tapper says "GOOSE!" — and the goose leaps up and chases them around the circle.
  5. The tapper runs for the goose&rsquo;s empty spot; if they sit first, the goose is the new tapper. If the goose catches them, the goose sits and the tapper goes again.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, the children sit in a ring with their knees together while one child runs around the outside — the dotted line shows the tapper&rsquo;s path around the circle.

Ask your child

"What does the tapper say on every head?" (duck) "What happens when they say goose?" (the goose chases) "Where does the tapper run?" (to the goose&rsquo;s empty spot)

What your child can say or do

Your child might stretch "duuuuck" for ten heads to build the suspense, pick their best friend as the goose every time, or run so hard around the ring that sitting down takes three tries.

Out in the real world

Birthday parties, family reunions, playgrounds at recess — duck, duck, goose is the game children run themselves, and now yours knows the whole script.

Try it together

Kind rules: the tapper walks, the goose runs, nobody catches anyone for the first three rounds. Goose-picker&rsquo;s honor: everyone gets picked within three rounds — the choosing is a kindness job.

Understanding check

Ask: "What word starts the chase?" (goose) "What do we do when we are sitting?" (hold still and wait)

This lesson pairs with the Duck, Duck, Goose flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Kids Games.
